subject: Post-call: CloudNova discovery + hyperscaler comparison & model-eval checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@cloudnova.com>, Suresh Rao <suresh.rao@helion.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next-step tests (CloudNova)

Hi Ava / Suresh —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Key takeaways
- CloudNova is evaluating inference options for a customer-facing summarization pipeline (200–600 tokens per request, heavy tail to 2k tokens for long transcripts).
- Primary concerns: 99th-pct latency under 400ms for short calls, predictable per-token cost, and hallucination risk on financial entities.
- You want a direct compare vs your current hyperscaler endpoint and a side-by-side on hallucination and throughput.

Proposed next tests (high level) — happy to refine:
1) Latency baseline (P95/P99) on short prompts (avg 250 tokens) — 1k requests distributed over 4 regions.
2) Throughput / tail testing with 8x concurrency, measure tokens/sec and GPU utilization.
3) Quality/regression: run our shared eval prompt set (attached eval-prompt-set-v1.csv) — measure hallucination rate, factuality, and answer consistency vs hyperscaler baseline.
4) Cost delta: run 10k token-sampled workload to estimate token cost and effective cost-per-response using batching/quantization suggestions.

Draft success criteria (for discussion)
- P99 latency <= 400ms on short prompts in us-west region under production-like qps.
- Hallucination rate on entity checks <= baseline + 2%.
- Cost per 1k tokens within 1.2x of current hyperscaler after enabling Redwood Optimize suggestions.

Who should own what (tentative):
- Redwood run the comparative benchmarks and provide raw logs + summarized dashboard (Ben / Marissa).
- CloudNova will provide a representative request sample and target SLA profile (Ava).
- Procurement loop for any contract/credits (procurement@cloudnova.com).

Attachments: cloudnova-discovery-notes.pdf, eval-prompt-set-v1.csv, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx

Next steps / proposed timing
- We’ll kick off a 2-week comparison window starting next Tue (2026-10-20) if that works.
- Internal kickoff: Ben/Marissa/Elliot to sync on test harness and required infra by Monday (10/19).

Ava — confirm the sample dataset availability and whether your hyperscaler baseline endpoint has any special headers/auth we should call out.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

---
Attachment stubs:
- eval-prompt-set-v1.csv (CSV, 120 rows: QA + entity-check prompts)
- cloudnova-discovery-notes.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)
- redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 2 tabs)

From: Ava Lopez <ava.lopez@cloudnova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudnova.com
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next-step tests (CloudNova)

Thanks Ben — this lines up with our notes. Confirming:
- We can provide a 5k-sample request set (anonymized) by COB Monday (10/19).
- Baseline endpoint: https://api.cloudnova.com/v1/generate (uses API-Key header). I’ll share a short-lived key with your team once we have an NDA in place.
- Procurement: we’ll loop in for credit discussion but prefer to run the comparison first.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you add a small hallucination probe focused on financial ticker/entity hallucinations? (We’ll add a few edge-case records.)
2) Please include a short note on how Redwood’s automatic prefix/KV caching would affect cost/latency for our transcript-heavy traffic.

The proposed start date 10/20 works. Looking forward to the kickoff.

–Ava
Ava Lopez
Head of Product, CloudNova
ava.lopez@cloudnova.com | +1 212-555-0203

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: CloudNova test matrix and owners (please review)

Marissa / Elliot —

Per Ava’s note we’re green to start the 2-week window on Tue 10/20. Please see a more detailed test matrix below; flag anything missing and volunteer for owners. I’ll coordinate logistics with CloudNova.

Test matrix (priority order)
A) Latency & tail (owner: Elliot) — start 10/20
- P95/P99 on short prompts (avg 250 tokens), target load: 1k rps bursts to emulate spikes.
- Record end-to-end time, token-gen time, and queue latency.
- Compare against CloudNova hyperscaler endpoint (they’ll share API key).

B) Quality / hallucination probe (owner: Marissa) — start 10/20
- Run eval-prompt-set-v1.csv (attached) plus the additional financial-entity probes Ava will provide.
- Metrics: hallucination rate (binary), factuality score (0–1), answer stability (same seed / prompt paraphrase).
- Provide example regressed outputs and diff against hyperscaler.

C) Throughput & GPU utilization (owner: Elliot) — start 10/21
- 8x concurrency stress tests; capture GPU mem, NVLink stats (if available), and batching efficiency.

D) Cost modeling (owner: Marissa / Ben) — deliverable: projected cost-per-1k-tokens under three configs (no batching, moderate batching, optimized with caching + quantization).

Technical notes to include in reports
- Redwood-specific controls: prefix/KV cache enabled for transcript reuse, continuous batching windows (configurable), and recommended quantization profile (int8-quant recommended for this model family).
- For hallucination checks, include exact prompt templates and answer-matching rules so we can reproduce on the CloudNova baseline.

Deliverables and timeline
- Test harness + baseline run by EOD Thu 10/22 (interim results).
- Full report (latency, quality, cost matrix, raw logs) by Tue 10/27.

Marissa — can you draft the hallucination probe rubric and a short runbook for reproducing any regressions?
Elliot — please confirm the harness (we’ll use k6 for request generation + a small GPU cluster in us-west).

Thanks — I’ll share the HubSpot link and Drive folder once created.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudNova test matrix and owners (please review)

Ben / Elliot —

I’ll own the quality/regression work. Quick confirmations and deliverables from my side: 

1) Hallucination rubric (deliverable: hallucination-rubric.md in Drive) — criteria:
   - Entity hallucination: any asserted entity (ticker, company name, monetary value) not present in source transcript or known public facts
   - Fabricated fact: new fact introduced that contradicts public records
   - Confidence thresholding: record model likelihood / logit-based proxy where available

2) Eval harness: I’ll run the provided eval-prompt-set-v1.csv + CloudNova’s 5k sample. I’ll also add 80 focused financial probes from Ava later this morning.

3) Regression workflow:
   - If hallucination delta > 2% vs baseline, produce 10 representative failures, templates, and suggested prompt/shot mitigations.
   - Tag model/quantization/config used and store raw responses in the Drive folder for audit.

Timeline: I’ll post interim quality dashboard by 10/22 EOD and final quality section in the 10/27 report.

On caching question: enabling prefix/KV cache should reduce per-response token generation by ~12–30% depending on transcript reuse. I’ll include an ablation in the cost modeling.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
